about: Velka's name stands before straight-quoted speech in which someone says 'He' about another man, and a name inside speech is followed by 'she said'; only the narration's pronouns may decide a gender.
title: The North Road
author: Tomas Reed

chapters.title: The Crossroads
paragraphs: Velka reached the crossroads before the rain. She dropped the pack by the milestone and sat down to wait.
"Ask Corin, he knows the road," Velka said when the cart stopped.
The drover looked down at the pack and the mud. "He went north at first light," he said.
Velka stood up. "He always goes north," said the drover's boy.
Corin came back along the north road an hour later. He was soaked to the knees and carried a lamp.
Velka waved the lamp over. "Corin, tell him he is wrong," she said, and pointed at the drover.
Corin laughed. He set the lamp on the milestone and shook the water from the coat.
The rain came at last, hard and grey. The four of them crowded under the cart. Nobody said a word for a long time.
Velka watched the road. She had walked it twice before and knew every stone of it.
"We leave at dawn," Corin said. He pulled the hat down over the eyes.
Velka frowned at the drover. "He snores," said the drover's boy.
Velka nodded. She was already asleep when the rain stopped.
The drover's boy kept watch until the lamp burned out. The road stayed empty. Somewhere far off a dog barked twice.
